subject: pe
title: Muscle Fibre Types
welcome_lead: Type I, IIa, IIx — the trio decides whether you sprint or marathon.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on slow and fast twitch fibres, recruitment and adaptation.
final_note: Fibre proportions are largely genetic — but training shifts characteristics within types.

concepts.def: Slow oxidative; high mitochondria, fatigue-resistant; endurance.
Fast glycolytic; large, powerful, fatigue rapidly; sprint/power.
Oxygen-binding protein, abundant in Type I (red colour).
Higher in Type I; supports aerobic ATP production.
Greater in Type II; correlates with peak force.

walkthroughs.body_html: Type I: slow, aerobic, fatigue-resistant. IIa: fast, mixed. IIx: fastest, anaerobic, rapid fatigue.
Low force: I only. Increasing force adds IIa then IIx via Henneman size principle.
Endurance training shifts IIx → IIa characteristics; detraining reverses. True I↔II conversion is limited.
